Shamsul Alam  ----- Petitioner

full_judgment: 8. Election Tribunal found 639 ballot papers in the packet containing ballot papers of the petitioner and 616 ballot papers in the packet containing ballot papers of the opposite party No. 1 exactly as shown in the result sheet of the disputed Subhapur School centre. Deduction of 33 ballot papers of the petitioner and 86 ballot papers of the opposite party No.1 on the ground of bearing no official seal can hardly be disputed and rightly not disputed by either of the parties and the same might have been counted due to oversight as there was no objection raised at the time of counting. As regards 332 ballot papers bearing double marks Election Tribunal has not noticed nature of the double marks. There is no finding that in addition to the petitioner in favour of which other candidate additional mark was given and by what kind of rubber stamp and what kind of ink; whether of the same or different size and ink. There is no finding that any of those double marked ballot papers were marked in favour of the opposite party No. 1 also. There is also no finding that any of the 99 cancelled ballot papers was illegally concealed though validly cast in favour of the opposite party No. 1. So the election petitioner opposite party No. 1 failed to establish his allegation that his many valid ballot papers were treated as invalid and counted as valid votes in favour of the petitioner or cancelled. It is true that presumption of correctness of the result declared by the Presiding Officer was lost as the Presiding Officer failed to show cancelled ballot papers in the result sheet. Since the 99 cancelled ballot papers did not contain a single ballot paper validly cast in favour of the opposite party No. 1 and votes counted in his favour were not increased, such incorrect result sheet is of no help to him. In such circumstances merely because the Presiding Officer did not show 99 cancelled ballot papers in the result sheet it cannot be inferred that 332 ballot papers were double marked at the time of counting the same by the Presiding Officer.
